You match readings by paraphrase. Below are a SENTENCE, the DEMAND inside it, and three numbered lists of readings of the DEMAND: A and B (from two auditors) and L (from a parser). Two readings match when they require, forbid or permit the same acts, each on its own or together in the same way, with every modifier applying to the same acts; wording does not matter. Pair the A and B readings that match, each A and each B reading in at most one pair. For each pair name the L reading that matches it, or NONE; each L reading in at most one pair. Then name every L reading in which a modifier applies to some of the joined items but not to an item between them (a skipped middle). Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer with one line per pair, `PAIR A<i> B<j> L<k>` or `PAIR A<i> B<j> NONE`, then exactly one line `SKIPPED: NONE` or `SKIPPED: L<k>, L<m>, ...`, and nothing else.

SENTENCE: 1. Everyone has the right to take part in the government of his country, directly or through freely chosen representatives.
DEMAND: Everyone has the right to take part in the government of his country, directly or through freely chosen representatives
In list L, {0} stands for everyone; {1} stands for the government of their country.
A1. Everyone has the right to take part in governing their own country both directly and through representatives they freely choose. Both ways are protected, and each person can use either one.
A2. Everyone has the right to take part in governing their own country in at least one of two ways: directly, or through representatives they freely choose. The right is met if either way is open to them, even if the other is not.
B1. Everyone has the right to take part in the government of their own country, and may choose how: directly, through representatives who were freely chosen, or both. Each way is protected separately.
B2. Everyone has the right to take part in the government of their own country in at least one of the two ways, directly or through freely chosen representatives. The right is met if one of these ways is available, even if the other is not, and the person does not get to pick which.
L1. {0} has the right to directly take part in {1}, and {0} has the right to take part in {1} through freely chosen representatives.
L2. {0} has the right to directly take part in {1} or to take part in {1} through freely chosen representatives, as one act done in any one of these ways (not each way on its own).
